references.text: Parallel account in Numbers where the Lord warns the Israelites not to go up to fight against the Amalekites and Canaanites, because He is not with them.
The Lord says that He will turn His face against them so that they are defeated by their enemies, showing the consequence of acting without the Lord's presence.
The Israelites could not stand against their enemies because they had sinned, demonstrating that God's presence is essential for victory.
Moses warns the people directly not to go up because the Lord is not in their midst, and they will be defeated by their enemies.
Moses emphasizes the importance of God's presence with the people, without which they should not move forward.
The Lord says that He will hide His face from them, and they will be consumed by many evils, showing the consequence of losing God's presence.
Gideon asks for a sign that the Lord is with him before he goes out to battle, illustrating the importance of God's presence in conflict.
